fixes.explanation: Gold and silver? Friend, nobody in this verse is passing around treasure. Moses says they "…did not meet you with food and water on your way out of Egypt…" (Deuteronomy 23:4). I once spent years in a drawer with zero snacks, so trust me, food and water are what you notice when they're missing.

Ha! I love it, but nobody's running a tent court here, friend. Moses says the LORD "…walks throughout your camp to protect you and deliver your enemies to you." (Deuteronomy 23:14). He's walking through the camp to protect them and hand over their enemies. I think that would be a comfort to hear when you're camped near an enemy.

A widow? Oh, baker, that's a swing and a miss, and I say that as a stamper who has swung and missed plenty. Moses says, "You may charge a foreigner interest, but not your brother…" (Deuteronomy 23:20). The widow never shows up in these verses. The two people on the scale are the brother and the foreigner.

Right, friend. Moses says you "…must not put any in your basket." (Deuteronomy 23:24). You may eat your fill of grapes, but the basket is where the answer is no. One verse, two rules, and you caught the one that says no.
